questions.prompt: On a 16 GB laptop, what context length does Ollama use by default, and why does it matter for agents?
questions.explain: Raise it with OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH when you start the server and verify with `ollama ps`.

options.text: About 4k tokens, far below the 64k that agents need, so the Pet forgets instructions
32k tokens, which is enough for most agent work, so the Pet needs no change at all
options.misconception: 32k is the default only with 24-48 GiB of video memory. A 16 GB laptop gets 4k, well below the 64k Ollama recommends for agents.

options.text: The model's own maximum, often 128k or more, so memory is the only limit you meet
options.misconception: The default is a memory-based tier, not the model's maximum. You raise it on purpose when you start the server.

options.text: 256k tokens, the largest default, so a laptop can run long agent sessions as is
options.misconception: 256k is the default only with 48 GiB or more of video memory. A 16 GB laptop gets the small default.

questions.prompt: Put the Pet's set-up in order.
questions.explain: Each step depends on the one before it.
items: Pull a model that lists tool support
Start the server with a larger context
Check what loaded with ollama ps

why.Pull a model that lists tool support: You need Ollama installed before you can pull a model.
why.Start the server with a larger context: Set the context when the server starts, after the model is on disk.
why.Check what loaded with ollama ps: Check after the server is up so you can see the real context and whether it spilled to CPU.
why.Start OpenCode: OpenCode comes last, once the model is running and sized correctly.
why.Install Ollama: Everything else depends on Ollama being installed.

questions.prompt: What is OpenCode's default permission policy?
questions.explain: Add an ask-everything rule first so the starting point is safe.

options.text: Allow everything, except reading .env files, which it asks about
Ask before every action, except reading files, which is allowed
options.misconception: The default is permissive, not cautious. You have to add the ask-everything rule yourself, first in the list.

options.text: Deny edits and shell commands until you allow each one in config
options.misconception: Nothing is denied by default. That is why you set the leash yourself.

options.text: Allow everything, including reading .env files, with no exceptions
options.misconception: Reading .env and .env.* files is set to ask by default, though the rest is allowed.

questions.prompt: This OpenCode rule list should stop `git push`. Rules are checked in order and the last match wins. Which line breaks the protection?
questions.explain: The last matching rule wins, so a broad allow placed after a deny cancels the deny.

lines.why: Just the start of the list.
This is the deny you want, but its position matters.
Just the end of the list.

questions.prompt: A small local model proposes running `rm -rf data/`. Who is supposed to stop it?
questions.explain: The tool's rules are the control. A model's good behaviour is not.

options.text: Your permission rules in the tool, not the model
The model, because a small model is cautious
options.misconception: A model's caution is not a control. Small models can propose destructive commands, so the rules in the tool have to catch them.

options.text: Nobody; local models cannot run commands
options.misconception: OpenCode runs shell commands with your authority regardless of which model asked for them.
